title: Horoscopi — the astrological manuscripts of Tycho Brahe
description: The astrological documents of Tycho Brahe whose primary form is a manuscript — the texts he wrote or had written for an astrological purpose and never sent to press — with every manuscript that carries them, the hand per witness with its authority, Dreyer's edition and the readable text where one exists; and the documents the sources attest but no one has located. The printed astrology, the weather diary, the Hven almanacs and the poem Urania Titani are bridged to their own pillars.

kinds.label: Nativity
kinds.gloss: A birth chart with its judgment (genitura, genethliacon, horoscopus).

kinds.label: Question
kinds.gloss: A reply to an astrological question put by a named person (quaestio).

kinds.label: Judgment on a comet
kinds.gloss: A judgment on what a comet portends.

kinds.label: Weather astrology
kinds.gloss: Tycho's own astrologia meteorologica: the planetary configurations of the year read for the weather, in an almanac or a treatise.

kinds.label: Star apparatus keyed to a nativity
kinds.gloss: A one-member class, named for what the one document is: a table of fixed-star positions computed for the Emperor's own nativity and appended to the star catalogue presented at his court.

KB.label: Det Kgl. Bibliotek

ONB.label: Österreichische Nationalbibliothek
ONB.note: The Austrian National Library. Codices 10686, 10688 and 10689 are the three bundles of Tycho's own papers that came to the Hofbibliothek with his effects; each is bound as numbered fascicles, catalogued in the Tabulae codicum (1864–1893) and in the library's online records.

items.title_as_given: Horoscopus Regis Christiani IV, ad mandatum Friderici II conscriptus in insula Hwena, a Tychone Brahe Ottonide Cal. Jul. 1577 (the title of the Copenhagen copies)

date.basis_note: subscribed on Hven on the Kalends of July 1577 (TBOO I p. 184)

subject.name: Christian IV, King of Denmark
subject.role: first-born son of Frederik II; king from 1588

birth.basis: born at Frederiksborg; the christening at Copenhagen on 2 June and the delivery of the nativity on 1 July are in the itinerary (Loca)

items.description: The nativity Tycho cast at King Frederik II's command for the prince born on 12 April 1577, subscribed on Hven on 1 July 1577 and delivered at Kronborg the same day. A full genethliacal treatise: the astronomical section with the figure of the birth, then the judgment by topic — temperament, the course of life, honours, journeys, marriage, death — with a German interpretation for the queen, as all three princely nativities carry. It survives in more copies than any other document of the register, all but one scribal: Tycho's own first draft, never finished, is among his papers in Vienna, and the copy handed to the king is lost. The Copenhagen copies call the subject king, a title he took only in 1588, so they were written after that year.

items.description: The nativity of the king's third son, prepared at the royal command in 1583, with a Latin preface that defends astrological prediction as physically grounded conjecture leaving free will intact. It survives in the presentation volume itself, in green velvet like its companion for Prince Ulrik. Which part is in Tycho's hand is contested between the two authorities this chapter has: Dreyer, who had the volume in hand, says only the German interpretation is his; the facsimile autopsy of the Graphonomicon finds the Latin chart, directions and judgment in his italic and leaves the German Kurrent open. Both are printed; neither is resolved here.

items.description: Beside the Latin book on the comet of 1577 Tycho wrote a short tract in German for general readers, to answer the many foolish German pamphlets on the comet, and it is here, not in the Latin book, that he discusses what the comet signified. items.title: The astrological and meteorological diary for 1573
items.title_as_given: Diarium astrologicum et metheorologicum Anni a nato Christo 1573 ad Loci Longitudinem graduum 35, Latitudinem graduum 56

date.basis_note: composed at Herrevad for the year 1573; the codex is dated 1572 and placed at Herrevad by the library

items.description: The almanac Tycho drew up for 1573 at Herrevad: figures of the heavens for the solstices, equinoxes and lunations, each judged for the coming weather, opening with a hard winter forecast from the solstice of December 1572. It is the only such diary of his that survives; the annual almanacs he later sent to Frederik II are all lost. He withheld it from the printed book on the new star, whose preface discusses it, and it was never printed before Dreyer. It survives in one manuscript, the presentation booklet as Tycho assembled it — the preface, the tract on the new star, the diary, the tract on the lunar eclipse and the elegy to Urania — of which only the eclipse tract is in his hand.

items.title: The appendix to the star catalogue keyed to Rudolf II's nativity (1600)

date.basis_note: Tycho's autograph dedication to Coraduz, 'Anno 1600 Mense Martio' (TBOO III p. 417)

subject.name: Rudolf II, Holy Roman Emperor
subject.role: the Emperor whose nativity the table serves

items.description: A supplement to the restored catalogue of a thousand fixed stars: thirty-six star positions adapted to the Emperor's own nativity, so that the new astronomy could be read into his horoscope — an act of court allegiance written into a scientific instrument. It exists in one copy only, the presentation volume of the catalogue that Tycho dedicated in his own hand to Rudolf Coraduz, the imperial vice-chancellor, in March 1600; the two companion volumes of the catalogue lack it. Dreyer printed it from this codex alone.

items.title: Tycho's nativity of himself — lost

date.basis_note: known only through the notes Stephanius copied from it

birth.basis: the Stephanius notes, copied from the lost nativity (Christianson 1970); Otte Brahe's memorandum has 'between nine and ten'

items.description: Tycho cast his own nativity; it does not survive. The notes Stephanius copied from it give the birth moment to the minute, 10.47 in the morning of 14 December 1546, which modern biography prints beside the father's memorandum. Von Späth erected the chart of 'Apollo' in Urania Titani from this recorded moment, so that reconstruction is not evidence for the lost document.

items.title: The Leipzig book of nativities, with Caspar Peucer's geniture — lost

date.basis_note: 'ante annos plus minus viginti quatuor' from 1588 (TBOO VII p. 137)

subject.name: Caspar Peucer
subject.role: Melanchthon's son-in-law; the geniture Tycho recalled in 1588

items.description: As a student at Leipzig Tycho kept a book of nativities. Writing to Peucer in September 1588 he reports finding in it, beside the scheme of Peucer's own geniture, the note he had made some twenty-four years before — Mercury in Aquarius in the third house, the Moon in Virgo in the ninth: a sharp and profound mind, and the misfortune of exile or prison that Peucer had since suffered. In the same letter he says he had been given to such predictions in his youth and had set them aside as his judgment grew and he saw the planets' places in the tables were wrong. The book still existed in 1588; it has not been located.

items.title: The annual almanacs for Frederik II — lost
items.title_as_given: 'the usual almanac' (the king's letter of 24 September 1587)

date.basis_note: a series; the last is asked for in September 1587

subject.name: the weather of each year, for the king

items.description: Among Tycho's duties to Frederik II was an annual almanac: a letter of the king dated 24 September 1587 reminds him to send the usual almanac for the coming year by the bearer, or as soon as it is ready. Dreyer, who knew the 1573 diary, states that none of the later diaries sent to the king is preserved, and that they must have been much shorter, giving only the planetary aspects' significations that touched the king. The 1573 diary is the sole survivor of the kind.
items.grade_basis: attested by the king's letter and by Dreyer; no witness known
items.what_would_settle_it: An almanac in the royal archives or among the papers of the Danish chancery for the years 1577–1587.

bridges.label: The Uraniborg weather diary, 1582–1597
bridges.home_holds: the whole diary as a scholarly edition: the day-by-day weather series and the historical notes, with the Vienna codex and its facsimile
bridges.why_not_here: it is the subject of its own pillar, and it is not in Tycho's hand: written on Hven by his assistants, who show no trace of his hand in it (Friis 1876). The old register counted it among his autograph documents.
bridges.facts: Vienna, ÖNB Cod. 10718: 191 leaves in quarto, 1 October 1582 to 22 April 1597; digitised. Edited by F. R. Friis in 1876 and again in Opera Omnia IX, pp. 1–146.

bridges.label: Morsing's Diarium astrologicum et meteorologicum for 1586, the first book from the Hven press
bridges.home_holds: the edition's bibliographical record after Nielsen, its press and its censused copies
bridges.why_not_here: a printed book by Tycho's assistant Elias Olsen Morsing, issued under Tycho's supervision with a preface he drafted; a printed edition is Typographica's atom, and its surviving copies are the census's. The old register listed it with no surviving copies, which read as if none survived.
bridges.facts: Nielsen no. 1170. Dedicated 1 January 1586, the calendar printed late in 1585. Nielsen names some twenty holding libraries; the census records twenty copies, fifteen of them located. Tycho's draft preface is readable in Scripta.

bridges.why_not_here: a printed book by Tycho's assistant Peder Jacobsen Flemløs, with a preface in Flemløs's name that the modern edition prints among Tycho's texts — the one text of the corpus in Danish. Typographica's atom.
bridges.facts: Nielsen no. 606 (Danish) and no. 607 (German). The censuses record two Danish copies attested and three German, one located. The preface is readable in Scripta.

bridges.label: De nova stella (1573): the astrological judgment on the new star and the preface on diaries
bridges.home_holds: the printed text with the Danish translation
bridges.why_not_here: printed by Tycho in 1573; a printed text is Scripta's atom. Its 'Astrologicum iudicium' on the star's effects and its preface, which explains the diary of 1573 and attacks the almanac-makers, are the printed face of the practice this register documents in manuscript.
bridges.facts: Opera Omnia I, the judgment p. 34, the preface pp. 35–44, the eclipse tract pp. 45–64.

bridges.label: The oration on the mathematical disciplines (1574): the defence of astrology
bridges.home_holds: the text of the oration with the Danish translation
bridges.why_not_here: delivered at Copenhagen in the autumn of 1574 and printed after Tycho's death; more than half of it defends astrology. Its manuscript is Cod. 10686/22 in Vienna. A text, and Scripta's.
bridges.facts: Opera Omnia I, pp. 143–173, with the editor's note on the two posthumous editions, p. 312.

bridges.label: The two commentaries on the comet of 1585, with their astrological conjectures
bridges.home_holds: both treatises with the Danish translation
bridges.why_not_here: the first was printed in Morsing's 1586 almanac under Morsing's name, the second Dreyer restored from Tycho's own drafts; both are texts and Scripta's. Their drafts are the largest block of astrological writing in Tycho's hand among the Vienna papers.
bridges.facts: Opera Omnia IV, pp. 397–414. Dreyer's notes (pp. 512–515) place the drafts in Cod. 10689: fascicles 23, 27, 30 and 44–45 (foll. 15–24) for the first treatise, and 18, 11 and 26 for the second, 'tota ipsius Tychonis manu scripta'.

bridges.label: 'Quae genera eventuum portendat crinita a. 1572' — Cod. 10689/41–46, fol. 21r–24v
bridges.home_holds: the commentaries on the comet of 1585, whose drafts Dreyer places on these leaves
bridges.why_not_here: the old register entered it as a judgment on the new star of 1572, on the strength of the title the Tabulae codicum gave the item. The library's record names no author. The leaves it occupies, fol. 21r–24v of the bundle, are among those Dreyer assigns to Tycho's drafts of the 1585 comet commentary (foll. 15–24 of fascicles 44–45). A witness of a printed text belongs to Scripta; the identification is stated as open until the leaves are read.
bridges.facts: Vienna, ÖNB Cod. 10689/41–46, a bundle of 28 leaves; the item at fol. 21r–24v, Latin, undated. Not digitised.

bridges.label: Urania Titani (1594): the poem in which four nativities are set
bridges.home_holds: the six hundred lines with Zeeberg's Danish translation
bridges.why_not_here: a poem, edited in Scripta and catalogued among the never-printed works in Typographica. The four horoscopes its allusions imply were computed by Ove von Späth in 1994; they are tabled below as reconstructions and counted nowhere. The old register entered them as four documents in four manuscripts, which counted this one codex four times.
bridges.facts: Vienna, ÖNB Cod. 10686/12: ten leaves in quarto, Latin, catalogued under Tycho's name — the poem's one manuscript witness.

bridges.why_not_here: the library catalogues it as 'Primae lineae germanicae alicuius genethliaci a quodam Tychonis Brahe discipulo' — the first draft of some nativity by a pupil of Tycho's. bridges.why_not_here: a letter; Epistolarium's. It is the attestation of the lost Leipzig book, and Tycho's own account of having set genethliacal prediction aside.

bridges.label: Ludolf Riddershusen to Tycho, 16 December 1599: questions on nativities
bridges.why_not_here: a letter; Epistolarium's. Riddershusen asks why so many with violent genitures die peacefully and so many with fortunate ones violently, and asks Tycho to resolve such questions.

bridges.label: Tycho to Riddershusen, 20 April 1600: on the nativities sent to him
bridges.why_not_here: a letter; Epistolarium's. Tycho replies that he will attend to the times and events of the nativities Riddershusen sent — the late practice of judging correspondents' genitures, of which no chart survives.

reconstructions.label: Titan — Erik Lange
reconstructions.subject: Erik Lange

birth_attested.basis: his birth data are unknown ('aldeles ukendt', Zeeberg 1994)

reconstructions.birth_reconstructed: 27 May 1554 — a date von Späth reconstructed from the poem's allusions

placements: Mercury 18°56' Gemini, retrograde, in the first house

reconstructions.reading: Mercury near Venus at the ascendant gives eloquence and charm; Mercury retrograde in the first house without a stabilising benefic signals inconstancy — the configuration Urania reads for proof of Titan's constancy exposes his instability. The poem's first horoscope.
reconstructions.basis: computed by Ove von Späth from allusions in the poem (Zeeberg 1994)

reconstructions.label: Urania — Sophie Brahe (two charts for her two candidate birth dates)
reconstructions.subject: Sophie Brahe

birth_attested.basis: the sources give both years; the arguments are nearly even (Familia)

reconstructions.birth_reconstructed: A: 22 September 1556; B: 24 August 1559 — von Späth erected a chart for each

placements: A: Sun 8°49' Libra in the first house
B: Sun 9°42' Virgo conjunct the ascendant

reconstructions.reading: Both charts give a Virgo ascendant, read as the precise, discriminating, serviceable Urania of the poem; the ascendant is the load-bearing signature whichever date is right.
reconstructions.basis: computed by Ove von Späth from allusions in the poem (Zeeberg 1994)

reconstructions.label: Tage Thott
reconstructions.subject: Tage Thott
reconstructions.birth_reconstructed: the chart erected for 28 May 1580, about 7.50 in the morning, at Eriksholm — the moment von Späth chose
reconstructions.reading: A Leo ascendant read as nobility and command: the trusted young nobleman who carries news between Urania and Titan. Sophie Brahe's only child, by Otte Thott of Eriksholm.
reconstructions.basis: computed by Ove von Späth from allusions in the poem (Zeeberg 1994)

reconstructions.label: Apollo — Tycho Brahe
reconstructions.subject: Tycho Brahe

birth_attested.basis: Tycho's own recorded birth moment (the Stephanius notes)

reconstructions.birth_reconstructed: erected from the recorded moment itself ('gengivet med det af ham selv fastsatte fødselstidspunkt', p. 313)

placements: Mars 11°1' Aries in the first house, in its own sign and angular

reconstructions.reading: An Aquarius ascendant read as intellectual vision; Mars in its own sign and angular as martial courage and mastery of instruments — the counterweight to Titan's chart. Because the chart was erected from Tycho's own birth time, its agreement with that time is not evidence of anything.
reconstructions.basis: computed by Ove von Späth from Tycho's recorded birth time (Zeeberg 1994)

desiderata: Cod. 10689/41–46, fol. 21r–24v: the leaves themselves. The Tabulae codicum title names a comet of 1572, Dreyer's notes place Tycho's 1585 comet drafts on the same leaves; only a reading settles which — and whether anything in the bundle concerns 1572 at all.
The draft nativity of Frederik II in Cod. 10686/17: whether it is in Tycho's hand, when it was written, and what it says. The fascicle is digitised and has not been read.
The reply to the Emperor's question in Cod. 10689/50: what was asked and what answered. Digitised; unread.
The hand of GKS 1823: Dreyer against the facsimile autopsy. A comparison of the German section against the wholly autograph GKS 1822 in the reading room.
Cod. 10689/29: the hand rests on the Hand’s own reading alone; an external palaeographic opinion is wanted, and the subject of the geniture is unidentified.

The Christian IV draft in Cod. 10688/8: the fascicle number is Dreyer's; the library's title for the fascicle ('Simplices motus a. 1576 etc.') does not name the draft. The fascicle should be read to confirm the draft is there and how far it runs.
Langebeks Excerpter 178–179: the horoscope copy is not itemised in the boxes' record; which box, and how much of the text, Langebek copied.

The eclipse prognostication of 1566, in which Tycho is said to have foretold the death of Sultan Süleyman: an explanation is attested (Dreyer 1890 p. 26), no document is located. Entered here, not as a record.
Duke Otto II of Braunschweig-Lüneburg asked Tycho for a nativity at Harburg in October 1598 (Loca, the Harburg call). Whether it was cast is not known.
David Fabricius's promised 'exempla nativitatum' (Opera Omnia VIII, p. 430): the letter is not yet keyed to the Epistolarium.
The German tract on the comet of 1577 has no modern edition or translation and is not in the Danish critical edition; it cannot be read here beyond Dreyer's text.
No photograph of GKS 1822, of the velvet bindings or of any horoscope leaf is in Iconographia.

Cod. 10688/17, 'Calculi miscelli, observationes, pericula' (1600), holds astrological directions in a hand the Graphonomicon grades possible; it has not been examined for a prose document and is not a record.
